title: The Confidence Manifold: Geometric Structure of Correctness Representations in Language Models (Cho, Wu, Da Costa, Koshiyama; arXiv 2602.08159v2, 29 Jul 2026)
sections_read: 2 Background (Linear Representation Hypothesis; Uncertainty vs. Correctness; Activation Steering; Problem Setting)
4 Experiments (Datasets; Models; Baselines; Probing protocol; Validation)
5.1 The Correctness Signal is 2-8 Dimensional (incl. What the dimensions encode is open)
5.3 What the Interventions Do and Do Not Show (incl. Comparison to a single-pass detector)

setup.data: Teacher-forced (question, given answer) pairs labeled correct/incorrect. Main: TruthfulQA (817 questions, paired correct/incorrect answers, misconception-heavy). Also SciQ, CommonsenseQA, FEVER, HaluEval (transfer); 640-1,280 samples per dataset; 300-600 paired samples per dataset in the Qwen2-7B per-dataset sweep. Steering: 200 TruthfulQA questions to fit the direction, n=617 held out. One judge-free own-generation test: multiple-choice CommonsenseQA (n=242 teacher-forced, n=199 own answers).
setup.models: 11 decoders, 124M-14B: GPT-2 (124M, 12L), GPT-2-Medium (355M, 24L), GPT-2-Large (774M, 36L) [base]; Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct (16L), Qwen2-1.5B-Instruct (28L), Gemma-2-2B-it (26L), Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct (28L), Qwen2-7B-Instruct (28L), Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 (32L), Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (32L), Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct (48L). All models below 1B are base, all at 1B or above instruction-tuned.
setup.positions_layers: Last-token residual stream at every layer; best layer chosen by CV test AUC (e.g. Qwen2-7B L20/28, Mistral-7B L23/32, Llama-3.1-8B L16/32, Qwen2.5-14B L32/48; GPT-2 family final layer). Steering adds the direction at every token position at the optimal layer during greedy generation.
setup.baselines: Output-based: P(True), NLL, token entropy, verbalized confidence, semantic entropy (K=5, DeBERTa NLI). Unsupervised: CCS, L2 norm, autoencoder reconstruction error, LOF, cluster uncertainty, pooled local intrinsic dimension (Yin et al.), LLM-Check Hidden Score. Linear alternatives: LDA, full-space difference of means.
setup.controls: GroupKFold by question (5 folds); preprocessing fit on training folds only; nested CV (outer 5, inner 3); random and orthogonal steering directions; length-only probe and length balancing; embedding-statistic correlations; paraphrase control (5 templates); contamination check (0/200 exact, 13/200 substring); seeds 42/123/456 for classification; RLACE and INLP erasure; DAS rank sweep.

key_results.claim: Two class centroids in a small supervised subspace match a trained probe and are label-efficient.
key_results.quote: two class centroids in a 2–8 dimensional subspace match a trained linear probe, and 25 labeled examples recover 90% of full-data AUC on GPT-2.

key_results.claim: Correctness of a given answer is linearly decodable across 11 models.
key_results.quote: A correctness probe reaches 0.80–0.97 AUC across the 11 models

key_results.claim: The discriminative subspace is low-rank: peaks at 2-8 PLS dimensions.
key_results.quote: Every model peaks between 2 and 8 dimensions and then degrades

key_results.claim: The mean shift exists in the raw residual stream; PLS only sharpens it.
key_results.quote: difference-of-means in the raw residual stream, with no projection, already reaches 0.72–0.91 AUC, and PLS adds only +0.034 to +0.081

key_results.claim: Classes are unimodal: multiple prototypes per class hurt.
key_results.quote: KMeans-2 and KMeans-3 within each class cost 1.3–2.4pp, so the per-class distributions behave as single unimodal clusters

key_results.claim: Steering along the learned direction changes error rate on Qwen2-7B by about 9 points.
key_results.quote: the error rate rises from 0.56 to 0.61 at α = −5 and falls to 0.52 at α = +5

key_results.claim: Random and orthogonal directions barely move the error rate at the extremes.
key_results.quote: random directions move the error rate by −0.8pp and orthogonal directions by −0.3pp

key_results.claim: Across six models the steering effect is 2.8-10pp.
key_results.quote: over all six, learned-direction effects run +2.8 to +10.0pp with specificity (learned minus orthogonal) of +4.1 to +9.6pp

key_results.claim: RLACE erasure drops detection AUC to chance.
key_results.quote: Across all 5 tested models this drops AUC to chance

key_results.claim: Rank bound comes from DAS alone.
key_results.quote: Peaks land at 1–5D and 4 of 5 models degrade at 32D, so for these models the causal effect is carried by at most 5 dimensions.

key_results.claim: Internal beats output only in the adversarial misconception regime.
key_results.quote: On TruthfulQA, output methods (P(True), token entropy, semantic entropy) fall to 0.44–0.64 while probes reach 0.80–0.94

key_results.claim: Why outputs fail there: the output reflects the model's belief, not correctness.
key_results.quote: the model confidently asserts the wrong answer, so any signal derived from the output distribution encodes the belief rather than its correctness.

key_results.claim: Single-dataset probes transfer near-randomly.
key_results.quote: A probe fit on TruthfulQA alone transfers close to random: 0.39–0.66 AUC on SciQ, CSQA, and FEVER

key_results.claim: Transfer failure is orientation, not absence.
key_results.quote: The failure is one of orientation, not of absence.

key_results.claim: A native HaluEval direction is near-orthogonal to the TruthfulQA one, and the transferred probe is below chance.
key_results.quote: refitting natively on HaluEval yields 0.99 in-domain AUC, and the two directions are essentially orthogonal (| cos θ| = 0.08)

key_results.claim: Below-chance transfer means a direction that is present but pointed elsewhere.
key_results.quote: a below-chance score is the signature of a direction that is present but pointed elsewhere.

key_results.claim: Optimal layer moves earlier with scale; mid-to-late depth for 1B+.
key_results.quote: the optimal layer moves earlier as models grow: the GPT-2 family peaks at its final layer, larger models at 46–75% depth

key_results.claim: Probes do not transfer between models; only the abstract structure is shared.
key_results.quote: What is shared across models is the abstract structure of the encoding, its dimensionality and mean-shift form, not the parameters of any particular probe.

key_results.claim: Layer choice matters far more than subspace dimension.
key_results.quote: Layer selection is 11× more impactful than dimension selection.

key_results.claim: P(True) is near chance on TruthfulQA but strong on standard QA.
key_results.quote: On TruthfulQA, P(True) drops to 0.48 (below chance) while centroid remains at 0.93, a +45.2pp gap.

key_results.claim: Iterative erasure leaves substantial signal in 7B models after 32 directions.
key_results.quote: After 32 iterations, AUC degrades substantially: GPT-2 0.58, GPT-2-Large 0.60, Qwen2-7B 0.75, Mistral-7B 0.72, Llama-3B 0.73.

key_results.claim: The teacher-forced detector loses 27 points on the model's own generated answers.
key_results.quote: the teacher-forced centroid detector reaches 0.957 AUC (n = 242) while the same subspace applied to the model's own generated answers reaches 0.688 (n = 199), a 27-point drop.

methods.name: PLS dimension sweep (discriminative dimensionality)
methods.what_it_measures: How many supervised directions are useful for separating correct from incorrect at a layer (AUC vs k).
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: 5 transformed (if the correct-answer subspace changes dimension or orientation under pressure); baseline geometry for 1 readout failure.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Steering along the PLS-1 direction; interchange on the k-dim subspace in the actual forward pass (not done here).
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Hundreds of labeled items per condition; last-token activations; seconds of CPU per layer.

methods.name: Two-centroid / difference-of-means classifier in PLS space
methods.what_it_measures: Whether class separation is a mean shift; label-efficient detector (25 labels for 90% of AUC on GPT-2).
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: 1 readout/threshold failure (centroids still separated under pressure while the output flips); group comparison of flipped vs resisted items as two clouds.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Add/subtract the centroid difference as a steering vector; project items onto it token by token.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Small labeled sets; standardize features first (unscaled DoM collapsed to 0.47 on GPT-2).

methods.name: Within-class multi-prototype and QDA test
methods.what_it_measures: Whether each class is one unimodal cluster (KMeans-2/3 prototypes per class; per-class covariance).
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Discrete states vs continuum: whether flipped items form their own cluster (separate fate) or lie along one axis.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: If a second cluster appears, test it separately with patching.

methods.name: Cross-condition transfer plus direction cosine and below-chance check
methods.what_it_measures: Whether a direction fit in one condition reads another; |cos| between natively fit directions; below-chance AUC as sign of a re-pointed direction.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: 5 transformed (frozen probe below chance, native refit high, low cosine) vs 6 erased (native refit also at chance); H3.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Multi-condition joint fitting; Procrustes alignment between condition-specific subspaces.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Labeled items in each condition (no pressure, pushback, tempting option).

methods.name: Cross-layer probe-weight cosine matrix
methods.what_it_measures: How the correctness direction rotates across depth (phase structure).
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Where along depth a correct-answer direction stops being continuous; supports subspace-path tracking across layers.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Choose layers for patching at phase boundaries.

methods.name: Levina-Bickel MLE intrinsic dimension by layer (pooled)
methods.what_it_measures: Dimensionality of the activation cloud regardless of labels.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Weak: pooled LID does not track correctness (AUC 0.51-0.58).

methods.name: Activation steering with random and orthogonal controls (specificity = learned minus orthogonal)
methods.what_it_measures: Whether adding the direction during generation changes error rate beyond a generic perturbation.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: 3 not routed (injection restores correct behavior) vs 2 bypass (injection does nothing); measures causal controllability, not endogenous mediation.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Generation runs over ~20 alpha values x n=617; a correctness judge (they used keyword overlap).

methods.name: RLACE / INLP erasure of the probe direction
methods.what_it_measures: Whether removing the direction(s) removes linear decodability.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Positive control for 6 erased (what decodability looks like after deliberate erasure); INLP residual shows redundancy.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Apply the same projection inside the forward pass to test behavior (not done here).

methods.name: DAS rank sweep on pre-extracted embeddings
methods.what_it_measures: Smallest rotated subspace whose interchange flips a trained classifier's prediction.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: As implemented, none causally: it tests a probe, not the model.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Re-run DAS with interchange inside the model's forward pass and score the model's answer.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Embeddings only (no GPU model loading) as done here; much more for true DAS.

methods.name: Teacher-forced vs own-generation evaluation (multiple choice)
methods.what_it_measures: Whether a detector fit on given answers works on the model's own answers.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Calibrates how much a teacher-forced correctness subspace transfers to our model-generated flips; H3.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Multiple-choice items so answers can be scored exactly.

controls_worth_copying: GroupKFold by question so no question appears in train and test; fit standardization and PLS on training folds only.
Nested CV for layer and dimension selection.
Random and orthogonal-to-direction steering controls, reported as specificity (learned minus orthogonal).
Full-space standardized difference-of-means baseline next to any projected method.
Output baselines on the same items (P(True), entropy, semantic entropy) and an unsupervised baseline (CCS).
Length-only probe and length balancing; correlation with norm, mean activation and sparsity.
Per-dataset native refit next to cross-dataset transfer, to separate absence from mis-orientation.
Judge-free multiple-choice test for own generations.

pitfalls.pitfall: Their DAS never touches the model: it is trained on stored embeddings to flip a classifier, so the 'causal rank at most 5' claim is about a probe, not the model's behavior.
pitfalls.quote: We apply DAS to pre-extracted embeddings at the optimal layer (no GPU model loading needed).

pitfalls.pitfall: The DAS objective flips a classifier prediction, not the model's answer.
pitfalls.quote: swapping the k-dimensional projected representation between correct/incorrect samples should flip the classifier prediction.

pitfalls.pitfall: Erasure shows necessity for detection only (decodability), not for behavior; and INLP leaves 0.72-0.75 after 32 removals in 7B models, so the signal is redundant beyond one direction.
pitfalls.quote: the subspace we identify is necessary for detection and not a redundant correlate

pitfalls.pitfall: Steering correctness is scored by keyword overlap, a weak judge.
pitfalls.quote: a generation is counted correct if the intersection of its tokens with TruthfulQA's correct-answer tokens exceeds its intersection with incorrect-answer tokens.

pitfalls.pitfall: Teacher-forced geometry does not carry over to the model's own answers (27-point drop).
pitfalls.quote: the teacher-forced centroid detector reaches 0.957 AUC (n = 242) while the same subspace applied to the model's own generated answers reaches 0.688 (n = 199), a 27-point drop.

pitfalls.pitfall: Scale and instruction tuning are confounded.
pitfalls.quote: every model we test below 1B is a base model and every model at 1B or above is instruction-tuned

pitfalls.pitfall: PLS fixes the subspace only up to rotation, so individual components have no meaning.
pitfalls.quote: a covariance-maximizing basis fixes the subspace only up to rotation within it, so no single PLS component has a semantics to read off

pitfalls.pitfall: 3D projections look overlapping even at AUC 0.91-0.93; do not judge separation by eye.
pitfalls.quote: Visual separation appears less distinct due to higher overlap in the projected 3D space, despite strong full-dimensional classification performance.

pitfalls.pitfall: Unscaled difference-of-means is dominated by high-norm dimensions.
pitfalls.quote: on raw embeddings it is dominated by high-norm dimensions

pitfalls.pitfall: Abstract overstates steering: 9.1 points is the Qwen2-7B number; the six-model range is 2.8-10.0pp.
pitfalls.quote: Steering shifts hallucination rates by 9.1 points on six models

pitfalls.pitfall: Internal inconsistency on dimensionality: elsewhere the paper says one direction suffices.
pitfalls.quote: a single direction suffices to extract the confidence signal

pitfalls.pitfall: LID baseline sign chosen on the full data (favors LID, but is a leakage pattern to avoid).
pitfalls.quote: the sign of −LID vs. +LID is chosen on the full dataset to maximize AUC

limitations_quote: the geometry is thus a property of the teacher-forced representation, and extending detection to free-form generations is open
future_work_quote: we leave free-form generative validation to future work once a trustworthy automatic judge is available

bears_on_fates.how: On TruthfulQA the internal centroid separates correct from incorrect answers (0.93) while P(True) is at chance (0.48): the information is decodable but the output-level readout reflects the model's belief. This is the static (no-pressure) version of 'scores lean right, output wrong'.

Below-chance transfer plus a high native refit and |cos|=0.08 between directions is their signature of 'present but pointed elsewhere'; the same check (frozen pressure-free probe below chance, refit high) would flag a transformed fate under pressure.
RLACE gives a positive control for what deliberate linear erasure looks like (AUC to ~0.5), but INLP shows residual signal after 32 removals, so 'erased' needs iterative and nonlinear checks.
Adding the correctness direction during generation shifts error rate by 2.8-10pp: injection has some effect, i.e. causal controllability, not evidence the model routes through it.
Nothing here tests whether the model's own answer uses the direction; the modest steering effect is compatible with the decision running mostly elsewhere.
Not addressed (no competing signal such as user pressure).

bears_on_group_angle: Mixed. Useful priors: the correctness signal in a given layer is a mean shift inside a 2-8D supervised subspace, classes are unimodal (extra prototypes hurt), and nonlinear or local classifiers add nothing, so a first group comparison of flipped vs resisted items can be two centroids in a PLS subspace rather than manifold machinery. Orientation matters more than dimension (intrinsic dimension explains R2=0.18 of AUC), and directions fit on different datasets are near-orthogonal; this argues for comparing subspace orientation across pressures (principal angles, joint fitting) for H1 rather than comparing dimensionality. Warnings: the 'manifold' in the title is a linear subspace; label-free manifold statistics (pooled LID, norms, LOF) do not carry correctness; 3D PLS pictures mislead; and the paper's causal rank claim rests on a DAS that only flips a probe. Probe-weight cosine across layers rotates gradually, which supports tracking a correct-answer subspace along depth, but they never track it across tokens.
architecture_location: Residual stream at the last token only; no attention-head or MLP localization. Best layer at 46-75% depth for 1B-14B instruction-tuned models (Qwen2-7B L20/28, Mistral-7B L23/32, Llama-3.1-8B L16/32, Qwen2.5-14B L32/48), final layer for GPT-2 base models. Intrinsic dimension compresses from 20-55D early to 8-12D at the optimal layer; probe directions change gradually across depth with nominal phase boundaries near 30% and 70%; Mistral re-expands at L30-32 after its optimal layer. The low-rank, mean-shift form is consistent across five families, but probe parameters do not transfer between models (GPT-2 to GPT-2-Medium 0.59, cross-family 0.44-0.48). Layer choice matters about 11x more than dimension.
actionable_fix: Monitor: a cheap two-centroid detector in a supervised low-rank subspace at mid-to-late depth, fit jointly on several datasets (single-dataset directions are mis-oriented elsewhere) and refit per model. Internal monitors pay off mainly where the model is confidently wrong (misconception-type items), where output confidence fails; on standard QA, P(True) is as good. For our project this implies that logit-margin or P(True) controls will look weakest exactly on confidently-wrong flips, and that a detector trained on no-pressure, teacher-forced items may lose a lot on the model's own pressured answers. Steering along the direction gives only small behavioral gains (2.8-10pp), so it is not a fix by itself.
reuse_verdict: adapt - reuse the protocol (GroupKFold by question, PLS sweep, standardized centroid baseline, random and orthogonal steering controls, per-condition native refit vs transfer, multiple-choice own-generation check) and the code; avoid citing their DAS or RLACE results as causal evidence about model behavior, and do not rely on teacher-forced probes for our model-generated flips.
relevance_to_project: Moderate, and less than the title suggests. It characterizes the static geometry of correctness for given answers (teacher-forced, single turn, no pressure, up to 14B), not what happens to that signal when the model acts against it, and its causal tests mostly act on probes rather than the model. Its value for us is as a baseline for what the correct-answer subspace should look like at 9B-14B (2-8D, mean shift, mid-to-late layers), plus two warnings that bear directly on H3: directions fit in one condition can be present but mis-oriented in another, and teacher-forced detectors drop 27 points on the model's own answers.
